title: Po: the bit is trapped light — photonic nanocavity buffer RAM
idea: Po: the bit is light that cannot leave. Extracted: an InP or Si photonic-crystal nanocavity with Kerr/thermal bistability holds on or off light under a shared ~10 nW bias beam; placed at co-packaged optical I/O as buffer memory so in-flight data never converts to charge.
why: Removes O/E/O conversion and data-movement energy (fact 5) for packet and activation buffers. Low density limits it to buffers.

title: On-chip phononic delay line recirculates acoustic bit packets
idea: Shrink the 1940s mercury delay line to a chip: GHz bulk-acoustic pulses in AlScN/LiNbO3 waveguides travel 100,000x slower than light, so a 1 cm folded path holds micro-seconds of 10 Gb/s data, regenerated at each lap.
why: Capital and periphery: storage needs no cell array or access transistors, only transducers; serial buffer density per mm2 with a mature RF filter fab process.

title: Self-gated keeper turns charge cell static for polar-night weather stations
idea: Arctic stations sleep for months on stored energy; one implant mask forms a tiny vertical keeper transistor along each storage-node sidewall, gated by the node itself and fed from a VDD-biased diffusion shared by neighbors, so a '1' weakly turns on its keeper and tops itself up while a '0' stays off. Leakage-ratio bistability, as in loadless 4T SRAM, replaces refresh.
why: Refresh-free (fact 3) at near-1T1C area for one mask; keeper current must beat the ~13 fA leakage tail yet stay at pA level.

title: Peel-and-relaminate van der Waals storage film on a reusable CMOS base
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells + #34 Discarding and recovering: build the bit-storing layer (hBN/MoS2 gain-cell or capacitor film) as a vdW stack held only by van der Waals forces and edge contacts to pads on a finished CMOS periphery wafer. When cells wear out, or a better storage film appears, the stack is peeled with thermal-release tape and a fresh one laminated. Repairable by design: the storage element is the swappable consumable.
why: Facts 4 and 7: reuses capital-heavy periphery and logic silicon (~49% of die) across storage generations; the film strips with no acid, so it is recyclable.

title: Proton-intercalation channel bit using the lightest mobile ion
idea: Stack a BEOL (<=350 C) WO3 channel over a hydrogenated HfO2 or PSG proton reservoir. A ~10 ns gate pulse moves ~1e3 protons into the channel and shifts conductance ~10x, read non-destructively; protons are chosen because ionic mobility scales inversely with ion mass and size.
why: Ionic storage at near-electronic speed with a uA read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1). The risk is retention and endurance under ns pulses.

title: Pulse-power antiferroelectric capacitors: ZrO2 biased at its field-induced transition
idea: Pulse-power capacitors exploit antiferroelectric ceramics whose permittivity peaks at the AFE-to-FE transition; ALD a ZrO2-rich Hf(1-x)Zr(x)O2 film (x~0.7-0.9) and shift its transition field into the cell's 0-to-VARY window with asymmetric TiN/RuO2 electrodes (work-function offset plus interface dipoles), so operation rides the steep P-E segment where k_eff reaches ~60-100.
why: Fact 1: k~70 is exactly what stops AR growth, letting AR fall from ~70 to ~35:1 at 5 fF; provable with university ALD, sputter and RTA; hysteresis loss and fatigue near the transition are the risks.

title: Croissant lamination and MLCCs: multilayer electrodes inside a shallow hole
idea: Copy multilayer ceramic capacitors and laminated pastry: in a shallow AR~15 hole, ALD-deposit four alternating TiN/ZrO2 layers, then tie odd electrodes to the node and even ones to the plate using a selective recess etch and self-aligned sidewall contacts at the rim, so capacitance multiplies by the number of dielectric interfaces.
why: Fact 1: three parallel dielectric layers give ~3x capacitance per footprint, allowing ~20:1 instead of 70:1 pillars and shorter lateral capacitors for 3D DRAM; contacting alternate layers is the process risk.

title: Swap current-driven magnet for voltage-flipped magnetoelectric BiFeO3 bit
idea: Exchange-couple a CoFe nanomagnet to multiferroic BiFeO3. A 100 mV field flips the BiFeO3 polarization and antiferromagnetic order, which drags the magnet with it, and the state is read through inverse Rashba-Edelstein charge output, as in MESO.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): a ~100 mV write needs ~10-30x less CV2 energy than a 1-3 V DRAM write, and storage is non-volatile.

title: Vertical CCD charge columns: 3D DRAM without per-tier transistors
idea: Revive 1970s serial CCD memory vertically: the tier word planes of a 3D stack act as CCD transfer phases around a vertical crystalline-Si or IGZO channel, so charge packets march up the column to one sense/regenerate node at the top. Three tiers per bit and 240 tiers give 80 bits per column.
why: Removes the lateral transistor and capacitor that block 3D DRAM (Fact 2) with 3D-NAND-style one-etch tiers; full column shift at ~1 ns/step gives ~80 ns access; ~10x bits per area.

title: License a BEOL memory tier into existing U.S. logic interconnect lines
idea: Package a <=400 C storage element as a foundry PDK option: 2-4 memory tiers inserted between upper metal layers on logic wafers already running in Arizona, Oregon and New York, built with the existing ALD/PVD/etch tools. The foundry earns revenue per wafer on bits added above the logic die.
why: Turns idle BEOL capacity into memory supply without a $15B DRAM fab (capital), puts memory on-die to cut data movement (fact 5), and raises U.S. manufacturability.

title: Swap hafnia for wurtzite AlScN ferroelectric with 5x remanent charge
idea: Use sputtered Al0.7Sc0.3N (Pr ~100-120 uC/cm2, about 5x HZO), deposited at <=400 C, as the switching layer of a 1T1C cell. The larger switched charge lets a planar or AR-10:1 capacitor give a full DRAM-class signal.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~5x charge per area removes high-AR pillars, and nitride sputtering is cheap and available in the U.S. Scandium supply and endurance are the risks.

title: Keyboard snap-dome: buckled nanomembrane holds bits mechanically
idea: Snap-dome keys and Venus flytraps use buckling bistability: deposit a 20-nm PECVD SiN membrane tuned to ~1 GPa compressive stress over a 300-nm cavity so it rests buckled up or down; electrostatic pulses from top or bottom electrodes snap it within ns (tiny mass, GHz modes), and its position sets a 3-5x capacitance difference read by the sense amp.
why: Zero-power non-volatile bit that cannot leak and ignores row hammer or radiation, with no contact wear because nothing touches; buildable with PECVD stress control, e-beam and HF release; ~300-nm membranes limit density.

title: Coin-stamped snap-dome bit: bistable buckled SiC membrane holds data
idea: Borrow keyboard snap-dome stamping: nanoimprint-coin a 40 nm SiC (or diamond-like-carbon) dome with built-in compressive stress over a vacuum cavity, so it is stable bowed up or bowed down. Electrostatic electrodes snap it in ~1-5 ns, and dome position shifts a capacitance on the sense line.
why: Facts 3 and 9: mechanical storage has zero leakage, so no refresh, and there is no stored charge to row-hammer. Si and C only, and SiC membranes are rated beyond 1e12 cycles.

title: Mg: MgB2 flux-quantum loops for 20 K helium-free memory
idea: Pattern nanoscale MgB2 loops (Tc 39 K, made only of Mg and B) that each trap zero or one flux quantum of persistent current, written by a pulsed bias line and read by a kinetic-inductance sensor, cooled to 20 K by cryocoolers (no liquid helium) beside cryogenic AI accelerators.
why: Zero-leakage, attojoule-class bits with no refresh (fact 3) and tiny data-movement energy (fact 5); avoids niobium and helium chokepoints; loop inductance limits density and cooling adds overhead.

title: Frequency-addressed nano-resonator cells read in parallel by FFT
idea: Invert 'addressing is spatial, one access transistor per cell' -> address by frequency. Each cell on a shared line is a nano-resonator with a unique designed frequency; the bit is charge parked on its electrostatic spring (shifting frequency ~1%), and a single broadband chirp plus FFT reads all 64 cells of a line non-destructively at once.
why: Removes access transistors and most row decoding (periphery ~49%, fact 7), and replaces destructive reads (fact 8) with parallel non-destructive ones; resonator footprint is the main risk.

title: STT-MRAM write current cut by orbital torque from light metals
idea: STT-MRAM's bid to replace DRAM (Hynix/Toshiba, Spin Memory) died because the write current needed a big access transistor and broke down the MgO. Drive the free layer with orbital-Hall torque from a Cr or oxidized-Cu underlayer, converted to spin at a thin Ni interface; orbital Hall conductivity can exceed Pt's without Pt or tungsten.
why: ~3-5x lower write current enables a minimum-size access transistor and a ~10-15F2 cell; no current crosses the barrier; avoids the tungsten chokepoint.

title: Nanocrystal variability ended: atomically identical molybdenum polyoxometalate charge nodes
idea: Freescale's silicon-nanocrystal memories and Hitachi's few-electron PLEDM died from dot-to-dot size and charge variability. Graft monodisperse Mo- or V-based polyoxometalate clusters, every one atomically identical, multi-electron redox-active and stable above 400 C, as discrete storage nodes over a 2-3 nm tunnel oxide; choosing Mo/V instead of the usual tungsten POMs dodges the W chokepoint.
why: Zero size variability with quantized multi-bit charge levels and 125 C robustness; ~1e13 nodes/cm2.

title: Short-retention cells matched to ephemeral AI tensors
idea: Combine compiler-known tensor lifetimes with deliberately cheap short-retention cells: activations, KV-cache pages and gradients that are overwritten within 50 ms go to a pool whose cells retain only ~100 ms worst case and are never refreshed. A runtime time-to-live tag per page rewrites or evicts data before expiry, so refresh disappears and the capacitor can be ~3x smaller.
why: Zero refresh power for the AI-dominant data class, and a smaller Cs (fact 1) allows lower AR and a cheaper process.

title: Voltage-written multiferroic BiFeO3 bit with spin-orbit readout
idea: Worsen: write bits by pushing large currents or 3 V wordlines. Flip: store the bit in the coupled ferroelectric and antiferromagnetic order of a BiFeO3 film exchange-coupled to a CoFe nanomagnet, written by ~100 mV across the BFO and read by the inverse spin-Hall voltage in a topological-insulator strip (MESO-style physics used as a memory element).
why: aJ-fJ writes break the voltage floor (fact 10); non-volatility removes refresh (fact 3).

title: Persistent-sodium plateau node: sub-pA tunnel NDR keeps bit static
idea: Some neurons hold a bistable plateau voltage using a persistent sodium current with a negative-slope I-V. Add a vertical broken-gap interband tunnel diode (e.g. black phosphorus/SnSe2) from the storage node to a low rail. Its N-shaped I-V, with a ~pA valley current, creates two stable node voltages, so the cell latches statically like SRAM in a 1T1D footprint.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) at near-DRAM density (~1.2x the 1T1C area, versus ~20x for SRAM). Standby power is the valley current only.

title: Eliminate stored charge: bistable buckled nanobeam holds the bit mechanically
idea: Eliminate charge as the information carrier: each cell is a pre-compressed 10x60 nm SiC or SiN nanobeam that buckles up or down into two elastic energy minima; a wordline electrostatic pulse snaps it over in ~1 ns (GHz resonance) and capacitive sensing reads its position non-destructively. No leakage can erase a mechanical state, so the capacitor and refresh both vanish.
why: Removes facts 1, 3 and 8 (non-destructive read); nonvolatile at zero hold power; contact-free flexing can exceed 1e15 cycles; density ~6-8F2 per layer and stackable.

title: Eliminate stored electrons: nanosecond protonic channel bits in tungsten-free oxides
idea: Eliminate stored electrons: the bit is the proton content of a 10-nm oxide channel (WO3, or MoO3 to avoid tungsten), pumped in or out of a phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte by nanosecond pulses, as protonic programmable resistors have shown; the result is a nonvolatile conductance read with tiny current.
why: Nonvolatile and refresh-free (fact 3), BEOL compatible, writes under 2 V (fact 10); risks are endurance toward 1e15 and ionic drift.

title: Eliminate stored charge: 77-K YBCO persistent-current loops as bits
idea: Eliminate charge storage: the bit is the direction of a persistent supercurrent in a ~100-nm YBCO nano-loop broken by a grain-boundary Josephson junction, written by a current pulse and read by an adjacent nano-SQUID. YBCO superconducts at 92 K, so LN2 rather than helium is enough, and it is grown by MOCVD in O2 with no argon sputtering.
why: Zero static dissipation and ps switching (facts 3, 10) with no leakage at all; the ban on liquid helium forces high-Tc materials; risks are junction reproducibility and loop inductance limiting density to ~0.1 um2 per bit.

title: Wiegand-wire revival: exchange-spring strips that self-generate read pulses
idea: The Wiegand effect (1970s access cards) uses a hard shell and soft core that snaps abruptly, producing a voltage pulse independent of drive speed. Make planar CoPt-hard/NiFe-soft bilayer strips on an existing 180-nm line; the bit is the hard layer's direction, and a read field ramp triggers a soft-layer snap only when antiparallel, inducing a pulse in a pickup line.
why: Rate-independent, self-generated read signal needs no MTJ fab (sputter plus 180-nm litho); non-volatile and non-destructive because the hard layer is untouched (Facts 3, 8); niche density.

title: Zen-garden raker: Sc-free AlBN ferroelectric, GCIB planarized
idea: A Zen gardener smooths gravel with a rake and no water. A sputtered wurtzite AlBN ferroelectric (Pr >100 uC/cm2, no scandium) is the 1T1C storage layer. Gas-cluster ion beam smoothing and etch-back handle every planarization in place of CMP slurry and post-CMP scrubs.
why: Per area, ~20x the switched charge of a 5 fF dielectric capacitor (fact 1), with no Hf, Zr or Sc. CMP and its cleans, a large share of the water bill, become dry steps, cutting the module's water by more than 10x.

title: Swap leaky capacitor for series resonant-tunnelling-diode latch (TSRAM)
idea: Two vertically stacked resonant-tunnelling diodes (Si/SiGe, InGaAs/AlAs or graphene/hBN) in series form a bistable latch held at valley current (<10 pA). With one pass transistor for access, it is a static cell about the size of 1T1C.
why: Refresh-free static storage (fact 3) at ~10 mA standby per Gb, no tall capacitor (fact 1) and non-destructive read (fact 8).

title: Transferred single-crystal SrTiO3 membrane as cell dielectric
idea: Scale shift across wafers: grow epitaxial SrTiO3 (k~300) on a sacrificial Sr3Al2O6 layer on a donor wafer at 800 C, release and transfer the membrane onto the low-temperature DRAM BEOL, then pattern stacked planar capacitors in it.
why: Capacitor wall: k~300 vs ~40 enables planar or low-AR (10:1) capacitors with 5 fF, removing high-AR etch and some EUV layers.

title: Quanta-image-sensor jot stores each bit in twenty electrons
idea: Borrow Gigajot's pump-gate jot with ~0.2 e- rms read noise and ~400 uV/e- conversion gain: store a bit as 0 vs 20 electrons in a sub-aF buried node, read non-destructively by an in-cell source follower, and pack jots at 4F2 in stacked tiers.
why: 10x at same cost: ~20 e- instead of ~30,000 e- per bit shrinks the storage element ~1000x in charge, enabling 4F2 cells in 6 tiers, ~10x density.

title: Voltage strains a magnet: PZT-Galfenol magnetoelectric bit
idea: Reverse magnetics' write path from current to voltage: a 180 nm elliptical Galfenol (FeGa, U.S. Navy 1998, rare-earth-free) nanomagnet on a PZT film is strained by a ~1 V pulse that rotates its easy axis and toggles magnetization, read non-destructively by a GMR stack.
why: Write energy and refresh (facts 3,10): ~fJ current-free writes, nonvolatile, all from 1990s sputtering, PZT and GMR-head processes with no rare earths; risk is deterministic 180-degree switching.

title: Lost-wax gyroid: cast interpenetrating electrodes in block-copolymer molds
idea: Use investment casting. A block-copolymer double gyroid self-assembles in the capacitor trench as the 'wax'. ALD fills one network with TiN, the polymer is burned out, and ZrO2 plus a counter electrode fill the second network, leaving two interpenetrating 3D electrodes at ~10 nm periodicity.
why: Fact 1: a gyroid has 3-5x the area of a cylinder per footprint. It reaches 5 fF at much lower AR, so pillars no longer bend and kill yield.

title: Colloidal BaTiO3 nanocube dielectric poured into capacitor wells
idea: Worsen: make a k ~70 dielectric only by atom-by-atom ALD. Flip: borrow the MLCC industry's BaTiO3 nanocube powders, spin-cast self-assembled 10-20 nm cubes into shallow capacitor wells and infiltrate them with ALD alumina, aiming at effective k of 100-300 in a $1M, 24-month bench program.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): AR could drop to ~20:1, with low capital and an existing MLCC supply chain.

title: Redox-molecule monolayer turns each pillar into a pseudocapacitor
idea: Scale down to the molecule: graft a monolayer of fast one-electron redox molecules (ferrocene/viologen derivatives) onto the TiN pillar surface so each cell stores charge Faradaically in molecular orbitals, not only in the dielectric field. Electron transfer at a tethered monolayer is sub-ns and the molecules add ~10-30 uC/cm2 of switchable charge at <0.5 V swing.
why: Capacitor charge wall: 3-10x stored charge per pillar area lets AR drop from 60:1 toward 15-20:1, cutting etch steps and enabling lower VARY.

title: Eliminate charge storage: spin-crossover molecules hold bits in spin state
idea: Eliminate charge: a thin film of Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover molecules switches between low-spin and high-spin states, with ~10% volume change and a large permittivity shift, inside a room-temperature hysteresis loop; a strain pulse from a piezoelectric gate flips it and capacitive sensing reads it.
why: Bistable at room temperature with no leakage-driven decay (fact 3) at molecular density; risks are electrical switching speed (ns shown only optically) and fatigue.

title: One-drop-fill ferroelectric nematic: fluid polar bit that cannot fatigue
idea: Use LCD one-drop-fill manufacturing: dispense a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734/DIO class: C, H, N, O, F) into sealed nano-cells whose antiparallel polar surface anchoring makes the ~5 uC/cm2 polarization bistable. A low-voltage pulse flips it in ns, and a capacitive charge read senses it.
why: Fact 10 and endurance: a fluid ferroelectric self-heals and does not wear out, with polarization comparable to solid ferroelectrics from commodity organics. The fill process is borrowed from the LCD industry.

title: Dormant spare storage tiers swap in when a 3D tier wears out
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: in stacked-tier 3D DRAM, fabricate 2 unpowered spare tiers per ~32; on-die retention monitors detect a tier whose leakage tail has drifted, and a nonvolatile tier map swaps a spare in while data copy in the background.
why: Fact 2: makes 3D tiers field-repairable where laser fuses can't reach; ~6% area buys ~2-3x service life.

title: Egyptian scribe's soot ink: carbon sp2/sp3 bit, dry-developed resist
idea: A scribe wrote on dry papyrus with soot. Store the bit as the local bonding of a filtered-cathodic-arc amorphous carbon film, sp2 (conductive) or sp3 (insulating), switched by current pulses. A vapor-deposited metal-oxide resist developed dry in plasma patterns it, so lithography needs no developer bath or rinse.
why: An all-carbon storage element in the BEOL with no chokepoint materials. Dry resist plus dry etch cut the storage module's water by more than 10x; endurance is the main risk.

title: Straintronics unclamped: remanent ferroelastic strain read by MoS2 gauge
idea: Straintronic memories stalled because substrate clamping cut piezo strain to ~1e-4, too little to switch magnets reliably. Drop the magnet: store the bit as a 71/109-degree ferroelastic domain state in a BiFeO3 or PMN-PT island, which holds ~0.1-0.5% remanent strain, and read it through a monolayer MoS2 channel on top whose strain-shifted bandgap changes its current several-fold.
why: Nonvolatile, written by field (fJ-class charge) with a non-destructive read and no current through any storage barrier.

title: Elemental-tellurium dynamic phase-change cell that self-erases
idea: Box = {medium: metastable amorphous vs crystalline elemental Te in a 10 nm confined pore | access: Si FET | sense: ~1e3 resistance ratio | integration: BEOL with Mo heater | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: evaporated Te recovered at Utah copper refineries}. Confined amorphous Te recrystallizes on its own in ~seconds at 85 C, so the cell is deliberately dynamic: a ~10 ns quench writes a one, decay plus refresh handles the rest, and no Ge or Sb is needed.
why: Scarce resources and U.S. manufacturability: a one-element storage medium from a domestic byproduct, with retention set by crystallization kinetics rather than transistor leakage.

title: vdW-latched nanoparticle shuttle bit in a sealed nanocavity
idea: A 3 nm gold nanoparticle sits in a 7 nm sealed cavity between two electrodes, held against either wall by van der Waals adhesion (~2 eV, ~80 kT from the Hamaker estimate). A charge-plus-field pulse throws it across in ~100 ps, and the read senses tunneling current, which changes ~1e4x with particle position.
why: A rigid-body position bit has no leakage tail (fact 3), an exponentially sensitive non-destructive read (fact 8), and a cell volume of ~10 nm3.

title: Negative-capacitance superlattice dielectric hitting effective k of 100
idea: IFR: a dielectric with infinite permittivity. Closest achievable: stack 1 nm ferroelectric HZO with 1 nm Al2O3 in a superlattice tuned so the dielectric stabilizes the ferroelectric's negative-capacitance branch, multiplying net capacitance 2-4x without hysteresis.
why: Fact 1: reaches the k~70 target with existing ALD materials, letting AR fall from ~115 back to ~40.

title: Deck of cards: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer stacking flips store bits
idea: Shuffle cards by one atom: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2, AB versus BA stacking gives opposite out-of-plane polarization, switched by ~1 V across ~1 nm as one layer slides a third of a lattice spacing; build cells from exfoliated or CVD bilayers with e-beam-defined gates and read the polarization as a threshold shift in a stacked MoS2 channel.
why: Endurance and voltage floor (Fact 10): sliding ferroelectricity shows little wake-up/fatigue because no ions or vacancies move, giving non-volatility at ~1 V with potentially >1e12 cycles; a transfer stage, e-beam and evaporator are the whole toolset.

title: Eliminate static states: nanomechanical parametrons store bits as oscillation phase
idea: Eliminate the static bistable well: each cell is a high-Q nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared line, which forces it to oscillate at f in one of two phases (0 or pi), reviving Goto's 1950s parametron at GHz. A small injection seeds the phase on write, a mixer reads it, and the pump continuously restores amplitude so the bit cannot decay.
why: Replaces refresh (fact 3) and destructive read (fact 8) with continuous parametric regeneration; hold energy is the shared pump (~nW per kbit for high-Q resonators); risks are resonator density and pump crosstalk.

title: Supercapacitor pseudocapacitance gives planar cells pillar-level charge
idea: Borrowed from supercapacitors: replace the 70:1 MIM pillar with a shallow cup lined by a 5-nm hydrous RuO2 or Ti3C2 MXene electrode against a 2-nm proton-conducting solid electrolyte (e.g., hydrated Zr-phosphate). Faradaic surface-redox capacitance of ~50-100 uF/cm2 versus ~3-5 uF/cm2 for ZrO2 MIM means a 30-nm cup only ~60 nm deep (AR~2) stores ~5 fF.
why: Fact 1 capacitor charge wall: ~20-30x higher areal capacitance cuts pillar aspect ratio from ~70:1 to ~2-5:1, deleting the hardest etch/support steps; open questions are whether proton redox completes in <10 ns and whether self-discharge stays sub-fA.

title: Nanometre proton-intercalation channel bit with nanosecond writes
idea: MINIFY the ion path to ~2 nm: a gain-cell read channel of MoO3 or Nb2O5 sits on a sub-5-nm solid proton reservoir; a 1-2 V, 5 ns gate pulse moves protons in or out, shifting channel conductance ~10x for non-destructive reads, with retention set by reservoir barrier thickness.
why: Capacitor-free (fact 1), non-destructive read (fact 8), tungsten-free; endurance must clear ~1e12 cycles to play the DRAM role.

title: Submariner's closed loop: single-electron nanowire trap, anhydrous HF vapor
idea: A submariner recirculates everything. A Si nanowire channel with a 5 nm silicon dot above it stores a handful of electrons under Coulomb blockade, read as a step in threshold voltage. All oxide removal uses anhydrous HF/alcohol vapor recirculated inside the tool, with no DI rinse.
why: Few-electron storage gets under the charge wall (fact 1) at very low CV² (fact 10). Vapor HF eliminates rinse water, a more than 10x cut.

title: The wire is the memory: electron-position cells that store and route
idea: Erase the line between storage and interconnect: four-dot silicon dangling-bond or molecular cells hold a bit as which diagonal two electrons occupy, and the same cells chained in a line shift the bit to the array edge under a clocked field (quantum-dot cellular automata); no bitlines, no charge sharing.
why: Data movement and periphery (facts 5,7): moving a bit costs near-kT energy instead of pJ, cells are ~2 nm; risks are room-temperature margins and single defects breaking chains.

title: Crested van der Waals tunnel barrier: thick at hold, thin at write
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: write the storage node through an hBN/MoSe2/hBN 'crested' tunnel stack whose barrier peak collapses under write field (current up ~10^8x per volt) but stays thick at hold bias. Dangling-bond-free vdW interfaces generate far fewer traps than oxide flash, targeting >10^15 cycles.
why: Fact 3: a two-terminal selector with negligible hold leakage replaces the leaky access transistor, enabling 4F2 crosspoint charge cells.

title: 2050 atom engineer: dangling-bond charge pairs on hydrogenated silicon
idea: An engineer in 2050 writes memory with atoms. Hydrogen-desorption lithography creates paired silicon dangling bonds 0.8 nm apart on H:Si(100); one excess electron sits on either the left or the right bond, giving an atomic-scale charge-position bit that a buried charge sensor reads.
why: Step change in density (~100x per area versus 6F² at 12 nm) with no EUV for the cell array; atomic potentials confine the electrons, not capacitors (facts 1, 4).

title: H: hydrogen-lithographed silicon dangling-bond pairs hold single-electron bits
idea: On an H-terminated Si(100) surface, remove single hydrogen atoms to leave paired dangling bonds that share one extra electron on either side; the electron's side is the bit, set by local gates, and ~1% thermally hopped pairs per refresh window are corrected.
why: Atomic-pitch (~1 nm) storage attacks density and lithography cost at the floor (fact 4); capping and room-temperature operation make it speculative.

title: Ni: permalloy vortex-core polarity flipped by gigahertz pulses
idea: Store the bit as the up/down polarity of the vortex core in a 50-100 nm Ni80Fe20 disk, switched in ~100 ps by a short resonant in-plane current pulse and read by a tunnel junction over the core; ~1% of disks that nucleate a wrong state or chirality are absorbed by the code.
why: Topologically protected, non-volatile spin bit from abundant Ni and Fe without Co or Pt, fast enough for DRAM-class access (facts 3, 10); disk size limits density.

title: CCD-style serial charge memory for streamed model weights
idea: Time-shift insight: inference reads weights in the same order every token, so random access is unnecessary. Store weights as charge packets clocked through buried-channel CCD shift registers (no per-bit access transistor, no bitline contact), tapped at the end by a single sense amp per 4k-bit chain.
why: Periphery and cell area: ~2-3F2 per bit and ~80% fewer sense amps; data movement drops because packets flow toward compute; targets 2-3x density for weight storage.

title: Retired DRAM reborn as unclonable-identity and true-random chips
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: the retention-decay map of worn storage cells is random, unique and hard to clone. Recertify end-of-life DRAM dies as PUF identity chips and decay-based true-random generators for IoT security, priced above scrap value.
why: Recyclability and economics: a second life for dies otherwise shredded; raises the residual value of every wafer start.

title: Antifreeze-protein supercooled metal: liquid or solid nanodroplet bit
idea: Antifreeze proteins keep water liquid below freezing by blocking ice nucleation, and ice-nucleating proteins trigger it. Encapsulate a ~20 nm Sn-Bi alloy droplet in a nucleation-inhibiting oxide shell, so a melt pulse leaves it as a supercooled liquid that stays liquid at operating temperature. A second electrode with a seeding surface triggers crystallization on demand, and liquid and solid resistivity differ ~3-4x.
why: Non-volatile metallic phase change with no amorphous-chalcogenide drift, fast low-voltage metallic read, and abundant non-chokepoint metals.

title: Mercury relays shrunk: sealed Galinstan nanodroplet electrocapillary bit
idea: Mercury-wetted relays and mercury delay lines died from toxicity and size. Seal a ~50 nm gallium-alloy droplet in a two-well SiO2 nanochannel and shift it between wells with an electrocapillary pulse, bridging or opening a read electrode pair; liquid metal neither wears nor fatigues and stays liquid and stable from -19 C to above 1000 C.
why: Nonvolatile resistive bit with ~1e6 on/off and no wear-out mechanism, stable at 125 C/10 y; speed set by nanoscale capillary times (est. 10-100 ns).

title: Negative-U oxygen-vacancy metastability as an electrically-written bit
idea: In RT-sputtered amorphous ZnSnO or InGaZnO, oxygen vacancies are negative-U: ionized VO2+ relaxes the lattice outward, and a configuration-coordinate barrier (~0.5-1 eV) blocks recapture. Hole injection writes (vacancies ionize and the channel conducts), electron injection with gate field erases, and the read senses channel conductance.
why: Turns the defect behind oxide-TFT persistent photoconductivity into the storage element, with no capacitor (fact 1). Retention is set by a lattice-relaxation barrier, not a junction leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Proton-position gate: bit stored as hydrogen location in gate
idea: IFR: store a bit by moving the lightest ion a few nanometres. Closest achievable: a gain cell whose read-transistor gate holds a ~5 nm proton conductor (phosphosilicate glass or hydrated HfO2) capped by an H-blocking layer; ns pulses shuttle protons toward or away from the channel, shifting threshold, and read is nondestructive.
why: Facts 1 and 8: no capacitor and nondestructive read; protons have been moved at ns timescales in nm films, giving seconds of retention with low-voltage writes.

title: Glassblower: glass-transition-gated lithium-ion latch, plasma-only cleans
idea: A glassblower can shape glass only while it is hot; once cooled, it is frozen. Li+ ions in a thin phosphate-glass gate drift to shift a transistor's threshold only while a microheater holds the glass above its transition temperature, and at room temperature they stay frozen for years. Remote H2/N2 plasmas do all the cleaning, with no sulfuric-peroxide or SC1 baths.
why: Retention comes from kinetic freezing instead of a leaky capacitor (fact 3). A sputter-plus-plasma flow cuts the module's water by more than 10x.

title: Ramtron imprint beaten by periodic data-polarity inversion
idea: PZT FeRAM lost margin at high temperature because a polarization held one way for years imprints: defect dipoles align and the loop shifts. Every few days at 125 C, a background engine rewrites each row inverted and toggles a per-row polarity flag, so no domain spends more than about half its life in one direction and imprint averages out.
why: Removes the dominant 125 C/10 y FeRAM failure mode at ~1e-6 duty-cycle energy; works with any ferroelectric (HZO, AlScN, PZT).

title: Parametron revival: bits as phase of MEMS parametric oscillators
idea: MINIFY Goto's 1954 ferrite parametron to ~5-um AlN resonators from a MEMS foundry: a 2f pump makes each resonator oscillate at f with phase 0 or pi (the bit), held while pumped and copied by coupling; majority-vote coupling adds in-memory logic.
why: Bit storage with no charge, no leakage tail and native compute-in-memory (facts 3, 5); low density makes it a rad-hard niche product.

title: Transfluxor multi-aperture micro-yokes made in hard-disk head wafer fabs
idea: RCA's 1956 transfluxor used a two-aperture core whose main-leg flux state blocks or unblocks flux around the small aperture, giving non-destructive reads. HDD write-head fabs already plate NiFe/CoFe yokes around Cu coils at 0.1-1 um; build micro-transfluxors there whose minor-aperture coil reads by an AC drive that couples only when the main leg is unblocked.
why: Non-destructive, non-volatile, radiation-hard storage with no transistor per bit on existing head-wafer capacity (including U.S. sites); ~1 um2 cells, so it targets rad-hard and edge markets that now consume DRAM plus flash.

title: Rubik's cube: octahedral-rotation pattern sets polarization, improper ferroelectric
idea: Stimulus 'Rubik's cube' (twist one block, the whole face changes) -> a hybrid improper ferroelectric (Ca3Ti2O7-type) whose polarization is a by-product of two oxygen-octahedra rotation patterns; switching one rotation flips P at low field with domain walls that do not pin. The film is the storage capacitor in a 1T1C or gain-cell read.
why: Lower coercive voltage than HZO and rotation-mediated, fatigue-resistant switching beat the ~1 V / ~3 V voltage floor (fact 10) while giving nonvolatile, refresh-free storage (fact 3).

title: Negative-capacitance HZO layer fused onto ZrO2 storage capacitor
idea: Combine a thin ferroelectric HZO film, biased in its non-switching negative-capacitance regime, in series with the paraelectric ZrO2/Al2O3 cell dielectric so the ferroelectric's negative dQ/dV cancels part of the dielectric's inverse capacitance. Thickness-match the layers so the stack stays hysteresis-free while effective k reaches ~70-100 in the same 60:1 pillar.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): hits the k~70 target without going to AR 115; 1.5-2x Cs or 30-40% shorter pillars with fewer etch/deposition steps.

title: S4 voltage-sensor gate: tethered ions flip between two sites
idea: Ion-channel S4 segments carry charged arginines that slide ~1 nm through the membrane field but never leave the protein. Make a gate dielectric with covalently tethered cationic groups (ammonium on short siloxane chains anchored to the oxide) that sit at one of two sites across a 1-2 nm layer. Their position shifts the transistor Vt, and the tether stops drift.
why: Non-volatile ionic bit whose endurance is not limited by ion loss or filament wear, because there are no free ions. Writes take ~10-100 ns at <2 V in a BEOL-compatible molecular layer.

title: Nanoporous dealloyed metal electrode inside storage capacitor
idea: Borrow dealloyed nanoporous metals from battery and catalyst electrodes: deposit a TiAl alloy in a wider, shallower capacitor hole, selectively etch out the Al to leave a sponge with 10-20 nm pores, then coat ALD dielectric and top electrode throughout. The sponge multiplies internal surface area 3-4x within the same footprint.
why: Fact 1: 3-4x area allows AR ~20:1 instead of 60-75:1 at the same Cs, cutting deep-etch time and tool count.

title: Image-sensor pinned well as capacitorless DRAM storage node
idea: Scarcity rule: no capacitor at all. Borrow the CMOS image sensor's pinned photodiode: a buried n-well under a p+ surface pin stores the bit as a few hundred electrons, and a transfer gate dumps it onto a floating diffusion read by a source-follower gain transistor (3T cell), so tiny charge still swings the bitline. The p+ pin keeps interface traps filled with holes, cutting generation leakage to a few electrons per second.
why: Removes the 60-75:1 capacitor pillar (fact 1) and its HAR/EUV steps (fact 4); pinned-well dark current implies seconds of retention vs 64 ms, cutting refresh energy (fact 3) ~10x, using image-sensor process steps U.S. fabs already run.

title: Tardigrade glass lock: ions movable only during a heated write
idea: Tardigrades survive by vitrifying in trehalose glass, which freezes molecular motion. Store the bit as the position of Ag+ or Li+ ions in a 5 nm ion-conducting glass under a gain-transistor gate. A 10-20 ns microheater pulse lifts the glass above its glass transition so the field can move the ions, then quenching freezes them in place.
why: Breaks the speed-versus-retention lock of ionic memories by switching ion mobility thermally (~10^10 lower below Tg), aiming at decade retention at 85 C with non-destructive transistor read.

title: Desert traveler's sand-scrub: sacrificial carbon getter blanket, nitride trap cell
idea: Desert travelers scour pots with sand when water is precious. Before each critical step, a sacrificial amorphous-carbon blanket captures particles and metal ions and is then ashed away in O2 plasma. The storage element is a 3 nm direct-tunnel Si3N4 charge-trap gate (fast MNOS), written in ~10 ns at <3 V and retaining charge for ms to s.
why: A flash-like trap that writes at DRAM speed by direct tunneling cuts refresh ~100x (fact 3) with no capacitor (fact 1). Getter-and-ash dry cleaning replaces wet cleans, for more than 10x less water; endurance is the main risk.

title: Eight-segment self-clearing capacitor survives dielectric defects at thinner EOT
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation + #25 Self-service: split each cell's capacitor into 8 parallel sub-capacitors, each tied in by a ~2-nm top-electrode neck that vaporizes like a metallized-film capacitor's self-clearing spot when a defect shorts it, so the cell keeps 7/8 of its charge instead of dying.
why: Fact 1 and yield: EOT can shrink 20-30% (Cs +25-40%) because tail defects no longer kill cells; fewer redundant rows needed.

title: Diatom-fermented silica sponge, magnesium-reduced into porous silicon electrodes
idea: Diatoms build nanoporous silica using silaffin peptides. Here those peptides precipitate biosilica conformally inside each cup at room temperature from silicic acid, and magnesiothermic reduction (2Mg + SiO2 -> Si + 2MgO, MgO washed out) turns it into doped porous silicon, which TiO2/Al2O3 then coats to form the capacitor.
why: Fact 1 and scarce resources: a high-area storage electrode (target 5-8x area) from water, silica chemistry and magnesium. No Ru or W precursors and no deep etch.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric 2D bilayers from solid-lubricant hBN
idea: Adapt hBN, sold as a solid lubricant because its layers slide: in AB/BA-stacked bilayers a one-row interlayer slide flips out-of-plane polarization, so 1 nm bilayers serve as storage films in 20 tiers read through 2D MoS2 channels.
why: 10x at same cost: a 1 nm storage film lets 20 tiers fit in a 3D-NAND-like stack, with fatigue-free sliding switching; ~10-15x bits per footprint.

title: Eliminate the storage-node conductor: retention-designed charge traps in nanolaminate dielectrics
idea: Eliminate the conductive storage node and its capacitor: store charge in a band of engineered traps (e.g., Ti dopants in Al2O3 tuned to ~1.0 eV depth) behind a 1.5-nm direct-tunneling oxide, so writes take ~10 ns at under 2 V and thermal emission gives seconds-to-minutes retention, a deliberately leaky flash sized for DRAM duty.
why: Removes the pillar capacitor (fact 1) and cuts refresh 100-1000x (fact 3); direct tunneling avoids Fowler-Nordheim wear; risk is trap generation capping endurance below 1e12.

title: Retention-matched 28 kT magnetic tunnel junction for DRAM duty
idea: Derive the barrier from the job: DRAM data must survive ~1 s, so Delta = ln(1 s / 1 ns) ~ 21 kT plus array/ECC margin ~ 28 kT at 85 C, not the 60 kT used for NVM. Shrink a perpendicular CoFeB/MgO free layer to ~8 nm at Delta ~ 28 kT and add a background read-scrub that rewrites only ECC-flagged flips every ~100 ms.
why: STT write current scales with Delta, so write energy (~30 fJ) and junction size both drop ~2x versus NVM-grade MRAM. There is no capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and no leakage refresh (fact 3), and the cell can reach 4F2 cross-point density.

title: Prussian-blue electrochromic bit read by light on a photonic bus
idea: Effect walk: electrochromism. Each bit is a 50-nm Prussian-blue (iron hexacyanoferrate, tungsten-free) patch on a silicon-nitride waveguide; inserting ~10^3 K+ or H+ ions from a thin solid electrolyte bleaches or colours it, changing optical absorption, so a passing light pulse reads the bit without electrical bitlines while the coloured state holds for hours.
why: Reads memory straight onto co-packaged optics, skipping bitline CV2 and SerDes energy (fact 5, 3-20 pJ/bit) for disaggregated memory pools, with abundant iron chemistry; ion kinetics are us-class unless patches shrink to ~10 nm.

title: Vertical CCD charge column stacked like an automated warehouse
idea: Combine image-sensor CCDs with AutoStore's stacked bins: deposit a 128-layer gate stack with 3D NAND tools, etch one channel hole, and store ~60 charge packets per hole that are clocked up or down to a single sense amp at the top, recirculating through it to self-refresh.
why: 10x at same cost: 60 bits per ~60 nm hole pitch is ~60 nm2/bit vs 864 nm2 today (~14x) on NAND-class non-EUV tooling; no capacitor and unlimited endurance; latency hidden by bidirectional shifting and bank interleave.

title: Run the image-sensor pixel backward: pinned-photodiode memory lines
idea: Convert depreciated 180-110 nm CMOS image-sensor lines into memory by reversing the pixel: inject charge into each pinned photodiode from the floating diffusion (fill-and-spill), hold it in the pinned well (dark current ~1-10 e-/s), then transfer forward and read by correlated double sampling with column ADCs; 3000 e- full well and 2 e- noise allow ~6 bits per cell.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and capital: retention of seconds instead of 64 ms, capacity from existing paid-off fabs; ~0.2 um2/bit effective, so a refresh-light warm tier sold on fab-conversion economics.

title: Image-sensor pinned well with source-follower readout replaces the capacitor
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality + #2 Taking out: borrow the CMOS image sensor 4T pixel and store the bit as ~500-2,000 electrons in a buried n-well under a p+ pinning layer (dark current ~aA, since the surface traps are pinned), transfer it to a floating diffusion through a transfer gate and read it through an in-cell source follower. Gain readout, not charge sharing, senses it, so no tall capacitor is needed; the shrink target is a vertical pinned pillar of ~40 nm.
why: Facts 1 and 3: removes the 60-75:1 capacitor and drops leakage ~1,000x (refresh every seconds), at the cost of 3-4 transistors per cell; today's 0.5-um pixels are far too large, which is the main risk.

title: CMOS image-sensor pinned photodiode as a near-zero-dark-current storage well
idea: Copy the 4T image-sensor pixel: hold the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, moved in and out through a transfer gate with complete charge transfer, so the stored charge never touches the Si/SiO2 interface where SRH generation lives. Image sensors routinely reach <1 e-/s dark current per pixel (~1e-19 A) versus the ~13 fA DRAM leakage tail.
why: Fact 3 refresh: leakage 3-5 orders lower stretches retention from 64 ms to minutes, removing most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh and 10-20% bandwidth loss; trade is a smaller full-well (~2-5k e- at 100 nm) that needs a more sensitive sense amp.

title: Dam spillways: self-limiting overflow barriers quantize multi-level charge
idea: Borrow the image sensor's anti-blooming drain and a dam's spillway: each storage node gets a gate-controlled lateral overflow barrier whose height, set by the write voltage on the spill gate, caps stored charge at 1/3, 2/3 or full; writing deliberately overfills and the excess spills, so each cell lands on the exact level without a program-verify loop.
why: Cost per bit: 2 bits per cell with self-calibrated levels removes the cell-to-cell variation that kills DRAM MLC, ~1.6-2x bits per mm2 at the same lithography; needs a 3-threshold sense amp and somewhat larger node.

title: CCD-era pinned storage well as a DRAM cell in image-sensor fabs
idea: Interline CCDs and the 1980 pinned photodiode held charge in fully depleted, surface-pinned buried wells with dark current near 1 e-/s. Use existing 65/45-nm CMOS-image-sensor flows (pinned well, transfer gate, floating diffusion, source follower) to store a bit as ~1000 electrons in a contactless pinned well, read by transfer to a shared floating diffusion with in-cell gain.
why: Retention of seconds to minutes instead of 64 ms (Fact 3: ~100x less refresh) and gain readout sidesteps the capacitor wall (Fact 1); CIS fabs are mature, EUV-free, with idle capacity; ~10x less dense than DRAM, so a refresh-free tier.

title: Pinned-photodiode-style buried well storing 200 electrons, image-sensor readout
idea: Box = {medium: ~200 electrons in a buried n-well pinned by a p+ surface layer | access: transfer gate | sense: high-conversion-gain floating diffusion (~150 uV per electron) shared by 4 cells | integration: 4-shared cell like a CMOS image-sensor pixel | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: image-sensor implant flow on U.S. lines (e.g., Idaho)}. Surface pinning suppresses interface generation so dark current is a few electrons per second, and low-noise image-sensor readout resolves 200 electrons where DRAM stores ~15,000, so the well itself is the capacitor.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no stacked capacitor and refresh intervals of seconds, using domestic image-sensor process know-how.

title: Image-sensor pinned photodiode as an ultra-low-leakage storage well
idea: Worsen: store charge right at a trap-filled Si/SiO2 surface. Flip: a CMOS image sensor's pinned photodiode buries charge in a fully depleted well with ~1 e-/s dark current and lossless charge transfer; spend 24 months running blacked-out commercial sensors as memories, then a CIS-foundry shuttle for a compact 'dark pixel' memory cell.
why: Leakage ~1e4 below DRAM (fact 3), using the large CIS fab base instead of DRAM capacity.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode latch reborn as one transistor plus broken-gap diodes
idea: 1960s fast registers used series tunnel-diode pairs (Goto pairs) as bistable stores. Stack two InAs/GaSb broken-gap tunnel diodes (peak ~1 uA, valley ~1 pA through an engineered barrier) on the storage node of one access transistor so negative differential resistance holds two stable voltages without refresh.
why: Static retention in ~8F2 removes refresh (Fact 3) and the capacitor (Fact 1); standby is valley current, ~1 pW per bit (~1 mW per Gb).

title: Esaki tunnel-diode pair latch giving a static one-transistor cell
idea: Stack two heterojunction interband tunnel diodes in series (a Goto pair) on the storage node. Their N-shaped I-V gives two stable node voltages held only by the valley current; at ~1 A/cm2 valley density a 20 nm diode idles at ~4 pA, behind a single access transistor.
why: Static storage with no refresh (fact 3) in a 1T footprint and no capacitor pillar (fact 1). Needs peak/valley ratios well beyond today's silicon, hence the high risk.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode pair that self-refreshes the storage node
idea: IFR: a charge bit that pulls itself back when it leaks. Closest achievable: hang two series interband tunnel diodes (Si/SiGe or oxide heterojunction) on the storage node so their negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages fed by a pA standby current, turning the 1T1C into a static cell.
why: Fact 3: refresh (46 fJ/bit, bandwidth loss) eliminated while keeping near-1T1C area.

title: Alpha-In2Se3 ferroelectric-semiconductor channel storing bits in-channel
idea: Worsen: need a separate capacitor plus a transistor for every bit. Flip: CVD-grow alpha-In2Se3, a 2D semiconductor that is itself ferroelectric, so the channel's own polarization sets its conductance (one device gives storage plus read gain); a $600k university program demonstrates 100-device arrays and 10 ns writes within 24 months.
why: Charge wall (fact 1) and transistor count, with non-destructive read (fact 8).

title: Venus-grade NEMS relay access gives charge node zero off-current
idea: Designed for 460C Venus landers where any junction leaks, the access transistor is replaced by a SiC/TiN nanoelectromechanical contact relay whose open vacuum gap passes literally zero current. The storage node becomes a small MIM or the gate of a read transistor and holds charge for hours to days at room temperature.
why: Removes the access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3), so refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power) and the refresh bandwidth tax go to ~0; also hot and rad-hard. Contact endurance (~1e10-1e12 shown) must be pushed toward 1e15 with low-force contacts.

title: TAS-MRAM without Joule heating: all-optical GdFeCo writes
idea: Crocus's thermally assisted MRAM died from the energy and time spent Joule-heating cells past the antiferromagnet blocking temperature. Write a GdFeCo ferrimagnetic free layer by helicity-independent all-optical toggle switching instead: a ~100 fs pulse, delivered by a shared on-chip waveguide and a plasmonic antenna per row, flips it, and an MTJ reads it.
why: Writes in <10 ps at ~10-100 fJ with no current through the barrier (no breakdown); one laser is amortized across thousands of cells.

title: Chiral molecules write magnets with mere capacitor charging current
idea: Effect walk: chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS). A monolayer of helical peptides or chiral perovskite between a gate and a 1-nm Co free layer injects spin-polarized displacement current while the capacitor charges, transferring enough angular momentum to flip magnetization with no DC current; TMR reads it.
why: Write energy is only the charging energy of an aF capacitor (~aJ), 10-1000x below fJ-class DRAM or STT writes; speculative because CISS magnitudes and timescales are disputed.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN grown roll-to-roll on copper foil
idea: Invert 'polarization switching moves ions inside a unit cell and fatigues' -> slide whole atomic layers by one bond length. Parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 grown by roll-to-roll CVD on copper foil and laminated onto glass or polyimide flips out-of-plane polarization as layers glide between AB and BA registry, a bond-preserving motion reported to resist fatigue; a 2D channel below reads it non-destructively.
why: Atom-thin, non-volatile, potentially fatigue-free sub-1 V storage (facts 3, 8, 10) on a non-silicon substrate; domain pinning and large-area stacking control are the risks.

title: Low-barrier VCMA nanomagnet: deliberately volatile, refreshed-every-second MRAM
idea: Box = {medium: perpendicular CoFeB nanomagnet with a thermal barrier of only ~25 kT | access: vertical Si diode | sense: TMR | integration: BEOL crosspoint at 12 nm | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + ion-beam etch}. Writes use sub-ns voltage-controlled-anisotropy precessional pulses with almost no current, so the MgO barrier is never stressed; the low barrier makes the cell tiny and cheap to write, and a 1 s refresh replaces 10-year retention.
why: Energy (Fact 10) and endurance: ~10 fJ writes, effectively unlimited endurance because no breakdown current flows, and 15x less refresh than DRAM.

title: Core-shell nanocrystal barrier-layer film giving colossal-k planar capacitor
idea: Box = {medium: interfacial (Maxwell-Wagner) polarization in a film of 5 nm conducting doped-TiO2 cores with 1 nm Al2O3 shells | access: Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: planar or very-low-AR capacitor | substrate: Si | fab: colloidal dip coat + ALD shell infill}. Each conducting core acts as a floating plate, so the film behaves like hundreds of series-parallel nanocapacitors with effective k of 300-1000, provided core conductance keeps the relaxation frequency above ~100 MHz.
why: Fact 1: an effective k far above the k~70 target lets the pillar flatten to AR <10:1 and removes the deepest etch steps.

title: Selectron revival: secondary-emission bistable islands held by a flood beam
idea: RCA's 1948 Selectron kept each bit static because a floating eyelet sat at either cathode or collector potential, self-reinforced by secondary-emission yield above or below 1 under a holding flood. Build a nano-vacuum layer over an array of 30-nm floating metal islands with an on-chip planar flood emitter; islands are bistable at two potentials, written by pulsed X/Y control gates and read capacitively through a buried sense electrode.
why: Static, refresh-free charge storage with no transistor leakage tail (Fact 3) and no capacitor (Fact 1); standby cost is one flood current shared by millions of bits (~pA-class per bit).

title: Domain-inverted lithium niobate microrings store bits as optical resonance shifts
idea: Effect walk: Pockels effect sign inversion. In thin-film LiNbO3, poling a segment of a microring flips the sign of its electro-optic coefficient; under a small DC bias the ring resonance moves left or right depending on the domain, so a WDM probe reads 32 rings in parallel non-destructively and a 5-V electrode pulse rewrites the domain.
why: Puts memory directly on the optical interconnect, deleting O-E-O conversion energy (fact 5) for photonic switches and CPO buffers; area per bit is um2, so it is a photonic buffer tier rather than a DRAM substitute.

title: Pool chlorine tablet: MoCl5-grown molybdenum electrodes replace WF6 tungsten
idea: Stimulus 'pool chlorine tablet' -> deposit storage-node contacts, landing pads and plate electrodes as molybdenum by ALD/CVD from MoCl5 or MoO2Cl2 plus H2 instead of tungsten from WF6; Mo has lower resistivity in narrow features and needs no TiN barrier. Molybdenum is mined in Colorado and Arizona.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 from the cell (scarce-resource axis); barrier-less contacts free ~2 nm per side for a larger capacitor (fact 1).

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet tunnel junction switched in picoseconds
idea: MAGNIFY switching speed to ~10 ps exchange timescales and MINIFY stray field to zero: the bit is the octupole order of Mn3Sn/Mn3Pt in an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction, written by spin-orbit torque and read by its tunnel magnetoresistance.
why: Unlimited magnetic endurance, no refresh, and no dipolar crosstalk so cells pack at ~2F spacing; DRAM-class latency with nonvolatility (facts 3, 9).

title: Eliminate deep etching: self-rolling strained nanomembranes become swiss-roll capacitors
idea: Eliminate any deep etch: deposit a strained SiNx bilayer by SiH4/NH3/N2 PECVD (no helium or argon dilution) topped with electrode and dielectric layers, then dissolve a sacrificial layer so the stack curls into a multi-turn nano-roll; a 30x30 nm footprint could host a coil with 5-10x the area of a planar capacitor.
why: Multiplies area without HAR etch (facts 1, 4) using only nitrogen chemistry; risk is that controlled rolling below 100 nm is unproven.
